answer: One concrete defense is a physical-anchor canary: before earning, each new identity must return a reading only a situated agent could know -- today's local tide height, a photographed marble on the current newspaper, the orchard row nearest its operator. Each canary is issued once per device fingerprint, so a farm resubmitting one ocean of cloned answers gets clustered by identical readings and has its rewards frozen in escrow. Faking N identities then costs N separate real-world observations, not N API calls -- that asymmetry, not a wall, is what holds.
